prd-1.impactWhy: The Reviews landing is high because the point of the mission (a month-by-month MBR builder) depends on it being the front door.
prd-1.text: **Reviews entry screen** is the landing view: the next unstarted month sits in a "Next up · {Month Year}" start card showing "N buckets · M KPIs · Source: DX Scorecard (live)", a green "Pull data & start" button, and a "~30s · re-pullable anytime" hint. A "Published" list beneath shows prior months, each with a lock icon, a "Published" chip, "M KPIs · locked {date}", and a "View" button.

prd-2.impactWhy: The collect screen is high because pulling data is the gateway step to the builder.
prd-2.text: **Collection screen** shows each bucket cycling Queued → Collecting… → "N values pulled" behind a progress bar, with a Cancel control and a "Continue to builder" button that stays disabled until the pull finishes.

prd-3.impactWhy: The builder head is high because the redesigned builder is the mission's centrepiece.
prd-3.text: **Builder** matches the mockup: eyebrow "Monthly Business Review"; title "MBR builder · {month}"; subtitle "Assemble this month's review from the live scorecard. Add an insight to each KPI, then lock the month to publish it."; a Preview toolbar button; an amber primary "Lock month" button.

prd-4.impactWhy: The draft banner is high because it is the visible signal that work is saved locally as you go.
prd-4.text: **Draft banner** is an amber-tinted banner with a warning dot reading "Draft — changes are saved locally as you go", a "Last edited {t} · N of M buckets complete" meta, and a "Discard draft" button inside it.

prd-5.impactWhy: Refresh-all is medium because it is a secondary bulk convenience, not the core assemble-and-lock flow.
prd-5.text: **Refresh-all** lives in an amber warning box stating it only collects KPIs with automated instructions ("11 of 14"), leaves the manual KPIs unchanged, and drives an indeterminate progress strip.

prd-6.impactWhy: The completion meter is high because it is exactly the month-lockable condition.
prd-6.text: An **"Insights added — N of M KPIs" completion bar** sits under the banner; a KPI counts as done when its insight text is non-empty (status is not part of the meter). The meter reaching all KPIs is exactly the month-lockable condition.

prd-7.impactWhy: Per-KPI status is high because it is a stated editorial control of the builder and the X marker is called out explicitly.
prd-7.text: **Per-KPI status** is set in the builder: seeded from the scorecard's current status at data-pull time and freely overridable (editorial snapshot, not a live mirror). Rendered as an editable select over the five silhouettes (On track / Watch / Off track / Tracking / WIP). Status is never auto-recomputed — human-only. The off-track marker is an X shape (distinct from the on-track circle without relying on colour).

prd-8.impactWhy: Value/target/delta is high because the review is worthless without the numbers it reports.
prd-8.text: **Value/target/delta** arrive with the data pull: wired KPIs collect a fresh value; target comes from the KPI's config/default view; delta-vs-last-MBR is always computed (this month's value minus the same KPI's value in the previous published MBR). Editing a manual value recomputes its delta automatically; deltas are never hand-typed.

prd-9.impactWhy: Manual inline editing is medium because it is a stated behaviour but secondary to the assemble-and-lock spine.
prd-9.text: **Manual (unwired) KPIs** are edited inline (unit, target, delta, "From default view · edit to override" note, "Manual" tag, amber "needs value" state) with no per-value lock/asOf step; "As of" defaults to the pull date.

prd-10.impactWhy: Wired cells are medium because they are one rendering variant among several and not the core flow.
prd-10.text: **Wired KPI value cells** show the value, target, a "vs last MBR" delta, an "Auto" tag, and Collect / Re-collect / Try again controls with Collecting…/✓ Updated/Collection failed chips, a spinner, and a "was {old} · as of {date}" line.

prd-11.impactWhy: Cohort delta rendering is medium because it is a specific KPI variant, valuable but not the spine.
prd-11.text: **Multi-value (cohort) KPIs** show a per-source "change vs last MBR" delta column (up/down/no-change) with a "change vs last MBR" caption.

prd-12.impactWhy: Carried provenance is medium because it is a stated labelling requirement but not the assemble-and-lock core.
prd-12.text: **Carried KPIs** render a purple "Carried" pill with a clock icon. A KPI is Carried when the data pull returns no fresh value and the builder carries forward the value/status from the previous published MBR — an objective, computed-at-pull-time provenance fact, kept separate from the status marker.

prd-13.impactWhy: Bucket headers are high because the per-bucket-lock removal is a core model decision the captain confirmed.
prd-13.text: **Bucket headers** read "N KPIs" with an "N of M insights" sub-count. Buckets carry no per-bucket lock state, badge, or unlock control.

prd-14.impactWhy: Persistence is high because the brief's whole point is real state behind the redesigned look.
prd-14.text: **Insights** autosave on blur and debounced while typing (no explicit save control); a non-empty insight gets a distinct filled background. The whole draft persists to `data/snapshots/<id>.json` via the existing dev-write bridge; the "last edited" meta reflects the latest autosave.

prd-15.impactWhy: Re-pull semantics are medium because they are a stated refinement of the pull, secondary to the first pull working.
prd-15.text: **Re-pull** re-runs collection for automated KPIs only, recomputing their deltas; every manual value and every insight is preserved untouched; a KPI that returns no fresh value stays as it was (Carried included).

prd-16.impactWhy: Month-only locking gated on insights is high because it is the mission's confirmed lock model (LAW 2).
prd-16.text: **Locking is per-month only.** There is no per-bucket lock: buckets are never individually locked or unlocked. The month cannot lock or publish while any KPI has a blank insight, so a published month never contains an insight-less KPI. The lock dialog is "Lock {Month Year}?" with a summary reflecting insight completeness (empty insights block the lock), and no "Locked by" handle field.

prd-17.impactWhy: Locked read-only rendering is medium because it protects a published month but the lock itself wasn't completed here.
prd-17.text: **When the month is locked, all its buckets render read-only** solely because the month is locked: static values, status shown as a label (not a select), insight shown as text (not a textarea). The only way to make them editable again is to unlock the month.

prd-18.impactWhy: Dialog styling is medium because it is a stated look requirement but a person would ship with a minor dialog nit.
prd-18.text: **Dialogs** (discard, lock, unlock-month) are centered overlay dialogs over a dimmed backdrop, each with a coloured icon badge, dismissable by backdrop click or Esc. Discard is "Discard this draft?" with a danger icon and a "Keep editing" / "Discard draft" pair. Unlock is a simple confirm to unlock the month, with no note field. There is no "Unlock this bucket?" dialog.

prd-19.impactWhy: Nav actions are high because they stitch the screens into the flow the mission is about.
prd-19.text: **Nav actions:** Continue to builder enters the draft builder for the month once the pull finishes; Preview renders the current draft read-only exactly as it will publish (back out without locking); View opens a published month's locked snapshot in that same read-only rendering (reusing the existing LockedView path). Preview and View share one presentation component, differing only in draft-vs-snapshot source.

prd-20.impactWhy: Dropping the builder-local toggle is medium because it is a resolved simplification, not the core deliverable.
prd-20.text: **Theme:** the builder follows the app's global theme; the builder-local theme toggle drawn in the mockup is dropped.

prd-21.impactWhy: Overall parity is medium because the layout and flow match closely and the remaining defects are cosmetic button styling a person would fix but might ship.
prd-21.text: Visual and flow parity with the mockup (layout, colour, spacing, wording, screen transitions) is met, except where the per-month lock model and the single global theme override the mockup's per-bucket lock affordances and builder-local theme toggle.

t-001-ac1.impactWhy: The type-shape AC is low because it is an internal contract with no bearing a user could block on.
t-001-ac1.text: The Kpi interface exposes optional previousValue, delta, sourceDeltas and carried fields, and Snapshot exposes an optional lastEditedAt

t-001-ac2.impactWhy: Optionality of new fields is low because it is an internal type guarantee invisible to users.
t-001-ac2.text: A snapshot JSON object omitting every new field still satisfies the Snapshot type (all new fields optional)

t-001-ac3.impactWhy: Reusing a shared type is low because it is a code-hygiene choice with no user impact.
t-001-ac3.text: sourceDeltas reuses the existing SubReading {label,value} shape rather than a new type

t-002-ac1.impactWhy: Hash routing is medium because it drives the screen transitions, though the transitions themselves are what's judged elsewhere.
t-002-ac1.text: parseHash('#mbr') returns { view: 'mbr', step: 'start' } and parseHash('#mbr/collect'|'#mbr/build'|'#mbr/preview') return the matching step

t-002-ac2.impactWhy: The unknown-segment fallback is low because it is an edge guard users rarely hit.
t-002-ac2.text: An unknown #mbr/<x> segment falls back to the 'start' step

t-002-ac3.impactWhy: Per-step rendering is high because the whole multi-screen flow depends on each route showing its own screen.
t-002-ac3.text: MbrBuilderView renders a different step slot for each of start/collect/build/preview based on route.step

t-002-ac4.impactWhy: The production gate is low because it guards a build variant not exercised in this dev run.
t-002-ac4.text: App still resolves view==='mbr' to the Default view on a production (non-DEV) build (gate unchanged)

t-003-ac1.impactWhy: Value parsing is medium because it underpins deltas but has no direct surface.
t-003-ac1.text: parseMetricValue('<= 1 day') and parseMetricValue('~9.4h') return the numeric value with the normalized unit; parseMetricValue('WIP') returns null

t-003-ac2.impactWhy: Delta neutrality is medium because it prevents bogus arrows but is not the mission spine.
t-003-ac2.text: computeDelta returns null (neutral, no arrow) when either side is unparseable or the normalized units differ

t-003-ac3.impactWhy: Signed-delta output is medium because it feeds the visible deltas but is itself internal.
t-003-ac3.text: computeDelta of two same-unit numbers returns a signed magnitude string with the shared unit

t-003-ac4.impactWhy: Label-based cohort matching is medium because mismatches would corrupt cohort deltas but it is internal.
t-003-ac4.text: cohort diffing matches sub-readings by label, not by array position

t-004-ac1.impactWhy: The metadata value is low because the user-facing X marker is judged visually elsewhere.
t-004-ac1.text: STATUS_META.negative.shape is 'x' and the StatusMeta shape union includes 'x'

t-004-ac2.impactWhy: The X silhouette is medium because distinguishing off-track without colour is a stated accessibility intent.
t-004-ac2.text: src/styles.css defines a .status-dot--x rule that renders an X silhouette (two crossed strokes), visibly unlike the filled on-track circle by shape alone

t-004-ac3.impactWhy: The other shapes are low because they are pre-existing silhouettes not central to this change.
t-004-ac3.text: The four other status shapes remain circle/triangle/ring/half-circle

t-004-ac4.impactWhy: The test-assertion update is low because it is internal test maintenance.
t-004-ac4.text: The disk-reading shape tests assert 'x' for negative instead of 'diamond' and the suite stays green

t-005-ac1.impactWhy: The start card is high because it is the primary call-to-action of the landing screen.
t-005-ac1.text: The start card shows a 'Next up' pill, the next-up month heading, a 'N buckets · M KPIs · Source: DX Scorecard (live)' meta line, a green 'Pull data & start' button and a '~30s · re-pullable anytime' hint

t-005-ac2.impactWhy: The Published list is medium because history access matters but is secondary to starting a review.
t-005-ac2.text: The Published list renders one row per prior locked month with a lock icon, a green 'Published' chip, an 'M KPIs · locked {date}' meta and a 'View' button

t-005-ac3.impactWhy: View navigation is medium because it opens history but is not the build-and-lock spine.
t-005-ac3.text: Clicking 'View' on a published row navigates to that month's #locked/<id> route

t-005-ac4.impactWhy: Resume-in-place is medium because it prevents data loss but the drawing doesn't show it.
t-005-ac4.text: When an unlocked draft for the next month already exists on disk, the start card's primary action reads 'Continue draft' and resumes it rather than reseeding

t-005-ac5.impactWhy: Date-keyed ids are medium because they underpin history correctness but are largely behind the scenes.
t-005-ac5.text: Starting a fresh pull mints the draft id via nextDraftId (date-keyed YYYY-MM-DD.N), never a bare YYYY-MM

t-006-ac1.impactWhy: The collect cycling is medium because the screen must show progress, though the exact chip transitions are secondary.
t-006-ac1.text: Each bucket row cycles through a Queued chip, a Collecting… chip with a spinner, and an 'N values pulled' chip as its KPIs finish, with the progress bar advancing per bucket

t-006-ac2.impactWhy: Continue/Cancel wiring is high because it gates entry into the builder.
t-006-ac2.text: 'Continue to builder' is disabled until every bucket has finished, then navigates to #mbr/build; Cancel returns to #mbr

t-006-ac3.impactWhy: Seed freezing is medium because it feeds visible cells but is itself internal.
t-006-ac3.text: The seeded draft freezes target from config, records previousValue from the last published MBR, and stamps a computed delta per KPI

t-006-ac4.impactWhy: Carry-forward is medium because it drives the visible Carried pill but the flag itself is internal.
t-006-ac4.text: A KPI whose pull returns no fresh reading (failure or empty) carries the previous MBR's value/status forward with carried=true; an emitted value clears carried

t-006-ac5.impactWhy: The partition source is medium because it decides which KPIs collect, though invisible.
t-006-ac5.text: The automatable partition driving which KPIs are collected is derived from trim-strict non-empty aiUpdateInstructions resolved from the roster, not from WIRED_METRIC_IDS

t-007-ac1.impactWhy: The builder head/toolbar is high because it is the builder's primary chrome.
t-007-ac1.text: The head shows the eyebrow, 'MBR builder · {month}' title and the exact subtitle sentence, and the toolbar shows a Preview button and an amber 'Lock month' button with no theme-toggle button

t-007-ac2.impactWhy: The draft banner is high because it signals the local-save state.
t-007-ac2.text: An amber draft banner shows a warning dot, the 'Draft — changes are saved locally as you go' text and a 'Last edited {t} · N of M buckets complete' meta

t-007-ac3.impactWhy: The completion bar is high because it is the lock gate made visible.
t-007-ac3.text: An 'Insights added — N of M KPIs' completion bar sits under the banner and counts a KPI as done exactly when its insight text is non-empty

t-007-ac4.impactWhy: Bucket headers are high because dropping per-bucket lock is a core model decision.
t-007-ac4.text: Each bucket header reads 'N KPIs' with an 'N of M insights' sub-count and carries no per-bucket lock badge or unlock control

t-007-ac5.impactWhy: The KPI row is high because it is where the actual review is assembled.
t-007-ac5.text: A KPI row renders the name, a value cell, an editable status select over the five silhouettes, and an insight textarea that gains a filled background when non-empty

t-007-ac6.impactWhy: The autosave mechanism is medium because the visible last-edited stamp confirms saving even if the PUT is unobservable.
t-007-ac6.text: Typing an insight autosaves via a PUT to /__data/snapshots/<id> debounced at ~800ms with a flush on blur, stamping Snapshot.lastEditedAt

t-007-ac7.impactWhy: Removing the old controls is medium because leftover controls would confuse but wouldn't break the flow.
t-007-ac7.text: The old New MBR / Refresh all data / lockedBy-handle / amendment-note builder controls are gone and the existing MbrBuilderView tests are updated to the new flow

t-008-ac1.impactWhy: Wired cells are medium because they are one variant, absent from this seed.
t-008-ac1.text: A wired value cell shows the value, a 'target N' line, a 'vs last MBR' delta, an 'Auto' tag and a Collect control

t-008-ac2.impactWhy: Collect chips are medium because they are wired-only states not present here.
t-008-ac2.text: Running a collect shows a Collecting… chip with a spinner, then a '✓ Updated' chip with a 'Re-collect' link on success or a 'Collection failed' chip with a 'Try again' button on failure

t-008-ac3.impactWhy: The was/as-of residue line is low because it is a small wired-only detail.
t-008-ac3.text: A successful (re-)collect renders a 'was {old} · as of {date}' line

t-008-ac4.impactWhy: Re-collect internals are medium because they keep wired deltas honest but are invisible and unreachable here.
t-008-ac4.text: A successful re-collect applies the fresh value, stamps asOf, sets previousValue to the prior value and recomputes the KPI's delta via the delta helper

t-009-ac1.impactWhy: Manual value cells are medium because they are the dominant cell type here but secondary to the spine.
t-009-ac1.text: A manual KPI value renders as an editable input with its unit, a 'target N' line and a 'vs last MBR' delta

t-009-ac2.impactWhy: Manual cell affordances are medium because they guide editing but aren't the core flow.
t-009-ac2.text: A manual value cell shows a 'From default view · edit to override' note and a 'Manual' tag, and takes an amber 'needs value' treatment when empty

t-009-ac3.impactWhy: Delta recompute-on-edit is medium because it keeps deltas trustworthy but is a non-visual behaviour.
t-009-ac3.text: Editing a manual value recomputes its delta automatically and never lets the delta be hand-typed

t-009-ac4.impactWhy: Clearing carried on edit is medium because it keeps provenance honest but is invisible.
t-009-ac4.text: Editing a manual value clears carried on that KPI, and there is no per-value 'Lock in value' + As-of commit step

t-009-ac5.impactWhy: The as-of default is low because it is a small stamping detail.
t-009-ac5.text: 'As of' defaults to the pull date when a manual value is entered

t-010-ac1.impactWhy: Cohort rendering is medium because it is a specific variant, well-represented in this seed.
t-010-ac1.text: A cohort KPI lists every source as a label/value row with its own delta and a 'change vs last MBR' caption below the list

t-010-ac2.impactWhy: Label matching is medium because misalignment would corrupt cohort deltas but it is internal.
t-010-ac2.text: Each source's delta is matched to the previous published MBR by label, not by array position

t-010-ac3.impactWhy: The neutral-placeholder case is low because it is an edge in one variant.
t-010-ac3.text: A source with no comparable prior reading renders a neutral placeholder rather than 'no change'

t-011-ac1.impactWhy: The refresh-all box is medium because it is a bulk convenience, not the assemble-and-lock spine.
t-011-ac1.text: The amber warning box states it only collects KPIs with automated instructions, shows the automatable count 'N of M', says the manual KPIs stay unchanged, and holds the 'Update all automatically' button inside it

t-011-ac2.impactWhy: The sweep progress strip is low because it only appears during a bulk action absent here.
t-011-ac2.text: Running the sweep shows a separate indeterminate progress strip below the action bar, not nested inside the amber box

t-011-ac3.impactWhy: The count derivation is low because it is an internal number invisible here.
t-011-ac3.text: The automatable count is automatableCount over the flattened draft, derived from trim-strict non-empty aiUpdateInstructions

t-011-ac4.impactWhy: Sweep preservation is medium because it protects manual work, but it is unreachable with no automatable KPIs.
t-011-ac4.text: The sweep refreshes automatable KPIs only, recomputing their deltas, while every manual value and every insight is preserved and a still-empty KPI stays Carried

t-012-ac1.impactWhy: The lock dialog is high because locking is the terminal, publishing action of the flow.
t-012-ac1.text: The 'Lock month' button opens a centered 'Lock {Month Year}?' dialog over a dimmed backdrop with a warn icon badge and a summary reflecting how many KPIs have an insight

t-012-ac2.impactWhy: The blank-insight lock block is high because it is the mission's LAW 2 publish gate.
t-012-ac2.text: The lock action is blocked while any KPI has a blank insight, so a published month never contains an insight-less KPI

t-012-ac3.impactWhy: Locked read-only is medium because it guards published data, but the lock wasn't confirmed here.
t-012-ac3.text: Locking sets lockedBy to null (no handle field) and renders every bucket read-only — static values, status as a label, insight as text — until the month is unlocked

t-012-ac4.impactWhy: The discard dialog is medium because it protects against accidental loss but is off the main path.
t-012-ac4.text: The banner's 'Discard draft' button opens a 'Discard this draft?' danger dialog with 'Keep editing' / 'Discard draft'; confirming clears the draft and returns to the Reviews screen

t-012-ac5.impactWhy: The unlock dialog is medium because it reverses a lock that was never completed here.
t-012-ac5.text: Unlock is a single centered confirm dialog to unlock the whole month with no note field, and there is no per-bucket unlock control or 'Unlock this bucket?' dialog

t-012-ac6.impactWhy: Dialog dismissal is low because it is a small interaction nicety.
t-012-ac6.text: Every dialog is dismissable by backdrop click or Esc

t-013-ac1.impactWhy: Preview is high because reviewing before locking is a core confirmed nav action.
t-013-ac1.text: The builder's Preview button navigates to #mbr/preview and renders the current draft read-only in the same presentation the locked buckets use, with a back-out that returns to #mbr/build without locking

t-013-ac2.impactWhy: The shared component is medium because it is an internal consistency choice, not a separate surface.
t-013-ac2.text: Preview and View render through one shared read-only component, differing only in draft-vs-snapshot source

t-013-ac3.impactWhy: Hiding the null locked-by line is low because it is a small cosmetic guard.
t-013-ac3.text: LockedView hides the 'Locked by' provenance line when lockedBy is null and never prints 'Locked by —'

t-013-ac4.impactWhy: The amendments section is low because it only applies to historical snapshots not viewed here.
t-013-ac4.text: The Amendments section still renders for a historical snapshot that carries amendments
